tools.name: box_list
tools.title: List boxes
tools.description: List your boxes with their names, states and images. For a connected client, client counts the boxes the user assigned to it and those it created, and max_boxes is how many it may create; with max_boxes 0 it may use only the assigned ones. view_url opens the box's screen for the person; hand it to them when a step needs them, such as a sign-in, 2FA, a captcha or a payment, and wait until they say they are done.

tools.name: box_status
tools.title: Show box status
tools.description: Show the state of your box: running or hibernated, its image, whether an upgrade is available, and when your files were last saved. view_url opens the box's screen for the person; hand it to them when a step needs them, such as a sign-in, 2FA, a captcha or a payment, and wait until they say they are done.

box.description: The box's name or id; without it, your first box.

tools.name: box_ensure
tools.title: Start or wake box
tools.description: Start or wake your box and wait until it is running. Waking takes a few seconds; creating a new box takes longer.

box.description: The box's name or id; without it, your first box.

tools.name: box_wake
tools.title: Wake box
tools.description: Wake your box, the same as box_ensure: start or wake it and wait until it is running.

box.description: The box's name or id; without it, your first box.

tools.name: box_create
tools.title: Create box
tools.description: Create another box with this name and wait until it is running. Your other boxes stay as they are; only a limited number may run at once.

image.description: An image family, such as cbdroid for an Android phone, or an image; without it, your usual desktop.

tools.name: box_hibernate
tools.title: Hibernate box
tools.description: Hibernate your box. Running programs and memory are kept and come back on the next wake.

box.description: The box's name or id; without it, your first box.

tools.name: box_save
tools.title: Save box
tools.description: Save your files, logins and agent history from the box to storage now. On a desktop box the browser closes during the save.

box.description: The box's name or id; without it, your first box.

tools.name: box_snapshots
tools.title: List box snapshots
tools.description: List the kept snapshots of your box's files, newest first, with when each was saved. The box may be hibernated.

box.description: The box's name or id; without it, your first box.

tools.name: box_restore_paths
tools.title: Restore files from snapshot
tools.description: Copy files or folders from a snapshot into a new folder ~/Restored/<save time> in the running box; nothing else changes. Paths are under ~ or /workspace.

box.description: The box's name or id; without it, your first box.

tools.name: box_upgrade
tools.title: Upgrade box
tools.description: Move your box to the latest image of its kind. Running programs restart; files, logins and agent history are kept. Requires confirm: true.

box.description: The box's name or id; without it, your first box.

tools.name: box_delete
tools.title: Delete box
tools.description: Delete one of your boxes with its saved state and snapshots. Requires the box and confirm: true.

box.description: The box's name or id; without it, your first box.

tools.name: usage
tools.title: Show model usage
tools.description: Show the model usage gw metered for your account, all your boxes together: requests, tokens and cost in micro-dollars today and this month (UTC), by model, with your daily cost cap (-1 unlimited) and what is left of it today. Your own model client's tokens are not in it.

tools.name: billing
tools.title: Show plan and credits
tools.description: Show your box plan, the credits left in your box wallet, when the paid period ends (0 without one), which boxes the plan includes (their machine time is free; other boxes pay from credits), a downgrade waiting for the period end if any, and the link to upgrade or top up. Hand the person billing_url when they run out of credits or want a bigger plan.

tools.name: box_view
tools.title: Show box screen
tools.description: Show the live screen of your box, waking it: a client that renders MCP Apps shows it in the chat, view only, with a button that opens view_url, where the person can type; elsewhere hand the person view_url. Use it when the person wants to watch, or a step needs them, such as a sign-in, 2FA, a captcha or a payment. Call it once per conversation; the view stays live. Other tools act on the box without calling this again.

box.description: The box's name or id; without it, your first box.

tools.name: box_view_token
tools.title: Mint a screen view token
tools.description: For the box screen view only: mints an hour's view-only token for the running box and names the socket that takes it.

box.description: The box's name or id; without it, your first box.

tools.name: box_approvals
tools.title: List pending approvals
tools.description: For the box screen view only: lists the connector calls of your boxes' agents that wait for your approval, oldest first.

tools.name: box_approval_token
tools.title: Mint an approval answer token
tools.description: For the box screen view only: turns the person's click on one of their pending approvals into a token, valid for a minute, that box_approval_answer takes. The token is in the result's _meta only.

tools.name: box_approval_answer
tools.title: Answer an approval
tools.description: For the box screen view only: answers one approval with the token box_approval_token minted for the person's click.

Run a bash command in the agent's persistent shell session (cwd /workspace). Returns merged stdout/stderr and the exit status; a non-zero status or a timeout is an error result. Output over ~30 KB keeps only its head and tail. Keep each command's wait well under the time left; save the required output early and improve it after.

tools.name: computer_act
tools.title: Act on screen

tools.description: Run one script for desktop work a single gui_plan cannot hold: loops over many items, data between apps, logic. A script is a JavaScript or TypeScript ES module run by Node 24 that drives the desktop through the desk API (import * as desk from '/opt/desk/lib/desk.mts': windows, accessibility snapshots with checked states, find and press elements, keys, typing, clicks, screen crops, gw model calls); the desk command does the same from shell. Pass code, or script: a file in the box. A module that exports main(params) is called with params and its return value comes back as result. Nothing persists between runs. Returns JSON {result, logs, error?: {kind, message}, duration_ms, exit_code, stderr, snapshot?, screenshot_path} and a screenshot taken after the run.

box.description: The box's name or id, as box_list lists them; without it, the default box.

code.description: The script as an ES module

max_edge.description: Scale the screenshot so its long edge is at most this many pixels, default 1024, 0 for full size; x,y then refer to the scaled image

params.description: Passed to the script's exported main(params)

screenshot.description: Return a screenshot taken after the run, default true

script.description: Path of a script file in the box; relative paths resolve under /workspace

timeout_s.description: Default 90, max 110; the run is stopped after it

tools.name: script_run
tools.title: Run automation script

tools.description:
Run a desktop-app GUI plan in ONE call: the box runs each step on the accessibility tree (0.1-0.5 s), checks it, and stops at the first surprise. Use it for GUI work in desktop apps (menus, toggles, dialogs, Preferences, Save As, settings). Write the whole plan at once, without looking first.
One op per step; optional window: title text of the window the step acts in (waited for):
{app: "mousepad"} focus or launch; {menu: "Edit > Preferences"} (an approximate path is fine); {menu: "Document > Word Wrap", on: true} set a menu toggle (read first, never toggled twice); {click: "Save"}; {check: "Show line numbers", on: false} a check box or switch; {set: "font size", value: "14"} a text, spin or combo field; {type: "text"}; {key: "ctrl+s"}; {wait: "Save As"} a window title; {verify: "Name", value: "x"} (or on, enabled); {close: true} close the focused dialog.
Returns {ok: true, trace} or {ok: false, escalate: {step, reason, window, outline}}. Trust ok: true: each step was verified, so add no checks or screenshots, except for the steps in caveats: read their effect first. On escalate, handle the reason, then call again with only the remaining steps. Close the dialogs you open. A path for a file dialog may end in \n to submit it. Name targets by their visible label.
A passing plan that starts with an app step is saved as a flow: name it with save: "app-action" and write values a later request changes as {{name}} with params: {name: value}. To save a plan that already ran, or the steps that passed before an escalation, call {save: "app-action"} alone: it does not run them again. Replay a flow with {flow: "name", params: {...}}: one call, no model. Check saved flows with {flows: true} before planning a task you may have done before. screenshot: true adds a screenshot (default: only on escalate).

box.description: The box's name or id, as box_list lists them; without it, the default box.

find.description: A request: returns the saved flow that does it

flow.description: Replay this saved flow instead of steps

flows.description: Return the saved flows, one line each, instead of running

save.description: Flow name for this plan, like mousepad-font-size; without steps, saves the last plan without running it again

steps.description: The plan, one op per step

tools.name: gui_plan
tools.title: Run GUI plan

tools.description: Read a web page without showing it: the box's Chrome loads the URL in a hidden tab with the user's cookies and sign-ins, waits for the page to load and its network to settle (at most 15 s, then returns what has loaded), and returns the page title, final URL and visible text, up to 20000 characters, then closes the tab. The user's windows and tabs are untouched. Prefer it to browser_navigate plus browser_read for looking something up. For reading only: to sign in, click, fill a form, or show the user a page, use browser_navigate.

For a form filled once per row, call it once per row.

fields.description: In order; each replaces the field's value

tools.description: One desktop call in plain JSON on the accessibility tree: op windows; snapshot {window?, text?}; find {name, role?, window?}; read {id, text?}; press {id} (selects, opens menus, clicks or runs the element's action); act {id, action: click|action|select|focus}; at {x, y, window?}; key {keys: "ctrl+shift+s"}; type {text}; click {x, y, button?, count?}; focus {window}; close {window}; launch {app}; shot {x?, y?, w?, h?}; screen. Element ids come from snapshot or find; window is title text, default the focused window. x, y, w, h and bounds are screen pixels, unlike computer_act's screenshot pixels. For GUI work of several steps use gui_plan.

box.description: The box's name or id, as box_list lists them; without it, the default box.
